message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell**.  
In many contexts the term **syncytium** (or **syncytial cell**) is used to describe a large, multinucleated cell that results from the fusion of several individual cells. A common example in pathology is the **multinucleated giant cell**, which forms during chronic inflammation or granulomatous disease.
